baseline.source: Exact delivered installer extracted and hash-verified against its manifest.

scope: Immediate target inclusion, fixed-setup registration with mixed 2D/3D links, progressive measured-colour rendering, compact analysis display and nonblocking legacy edited-project inventory.

coverage: actual picked sphere API immediately inserts usable target row
finite sphere/checker RMS above old thresholds retained with numeric quality warnings
pending legacy target migration respects rejected/off targets
any fixed setup in either component retains exact current pose
rotated vertical group adjusted with an external anchor
independent checks and explicit exclusions retained
registration above residual tolerance still applied with residual report
virtual poses and immutable original XYZ; no duplicate cloud allocation

findings.title: Register setups rollback did not cover draft creation/removal
reproduced: cancel before commit retained new draft
failed new solve removed prior draft
findings.fix: Root added complete STATE and SELECTION rollback around solve plus accept.

findings.title: Re-solving an existing rotated vertical edge replaced its stored up axis with world Z
findings.reproduced: A-B and B-C 2D links rotated together by A-D 3D registration; rerunning A-B 2D then raised inconsistent vertical directions.
findings.fix: Root preserves and validates the existing vertical edge axis when replacing that edge in vertical mode.

positive_coverage: successful API action has one Undo checkpoint and exact Undo/Redo
original XYZ/attribute files and file inventory unchanged by virtual registration
cancel, solve failure, save failure and mid-Apply failure restore complete state and history
non-finite and collinear correspondences cannot apply a transform
noisy four-setup loop with two differently oriented vertical groups retains exact constraints
each of four selected fixed setups retains its existing pose exactly
re-solving an existing rotated 2D edge retains its up axis
limitations: Production API, solver and history code with controlled synchronous job execution
Native Windows process scheduling and WebView2 not exercised by this independent pass
UI source reviewed; browser scenarios were run by the UI author separately

registration_browser.platform: Linux Chromium141, controlled API responses, actual production registration markup/scripts.

scenarios: No hidden overview, section or registration preview requests
Setup opens on coloured coarse perspective points while fine response is held
Refresh point detail retries a failed response without requiring camera movement
Fine response preserves measured coordinates and RGB colours
Drag automatically requests one coalesced quick/fine detail pair
Wheel reuses covering detail and automatically loads a wider view
Wider viewport automatically refreshes horizontal perspective detail
Late response from previous setup cannot overwrite current setup
Repeated selection clear performs zero point-buffer uploads
Legacy remaining count refreshes automatically without geometry requests or GPU uploads
Binary analysis equals JSON colours, avoids flattening, uploads once per recolour
Background count completion preserves the active analysis layer and GPU buffer
Late normal scan response cannot replace an active analysis overlay
Restore from analysis resumes missing fine detail after aborted load
Pending deletion stays hidden through selection clear; failure restores source display
render_browser.fixture: Two synthetic four-point setups; delayed binary responses are controlled. This is not a large-cloud throughput benchmark.

counts_overlap: Focused numerical, storage and backend suites are included in the 386-test application run. Browser scenarios and 83 installer tests are separate; do not sum overlapping focused counts.

backend_view_detail.limitations: Synthetic real files on Linux with filesystem cache; not a Windows/GPU or billion-point benchmark.

legacy_inventory.limitations: Synthetic real files on Linux with filesystem cache; wall time may include concurrent release verification. This measures backend inventory, not browser, Windows, GPU, or billion-point performance.

analysis_response_preparation.baseline: Exact preview functions extracted from delivered 0.18.5 installer; compact JSON encoding matches server.Handler.send.
analysis_response_preparation.scope: Preview sampling, colour preparation and response serialization. Saved analytical record generation/comparison computation and GPU rendering excluded. OS filesystem cache is warm.

analysis_response_browser.scope: Loopback HTTP response transfer and body read plus browser decode/display-array construction. Static prebuilt responses isolate transport and decoding from server preparation. Analytical computation, GPU upload/render and Windows WebView2 excluded. One warm-up and explicit GC before each measured run.

preserved_behavior: Registration applies virtual setup poses without modifying original XYZ/attributes or allocating a duplicate merged cloud.
Original stored comparison data, Float64 deviations/statistics and exports are unchanged by compact display transport.
Independent Check targets and explicit Exclude/rejected roles remain separate from Fit targets.
Pending point deletion stays hidden after clearing selection; failed deletion restores original display.
Exact analytical/editing properties remain separate from conservative inventory display metadata.
Earlier whole-input geometry/range, grouping/deletion, project storage, startup and installer lifecycle fixes remain in cumulative source and regression gates.
release_packaging_gates: Verify all 20,001 Windows runtime files against the exact 0.18.5 manifest.
Run the actual production component/startup command on staged application and the isolated 21 MB recovery fixture before building.
Run installer/lifecycle tests again from staged build support and isolated bootstrap helper imports.
Verify staging manifest before and after NSIS build.
Independently extract completed EXE, compare all manifest members and frozen source hashes, verify executable version/architecture and bootstrap/uninstaller inventory.
Run the actual production component/startup command against extracted application; final gate results are recorded alongside the completed installer.
runtime_policy: No bundled Windows runtime files changed. Linux validation packages are not replacements for the Windows payload.
limitations: Synthetic numerical/storage fixtures and Linux Chromium tests do not establish survey accuracy for the user tunnel.
Native Windows installation/registry, WebView2, workstation GPU and cold-disk loading were not executed on this build host.
The viewport display budget remains bounded at up to 1 million points; this does not cap retained originals processed by full-input analytical workflows.
Rendering benchmarks measure the named stage only. Browser/server medians are separate experiments and must not be added into a total latency claim.
No instantaneous whole-tunnel computation, universal 7 GB memory cap or 350-million-to-five-billion-point end-to-end benchmark is claimed.
Semantic segment classification and bolt detection still require validation against representative user data; this release does not certify every historical reported issue fixed.
